utterances.text: Well, no. Because we were supposed to agree on this with the Croat side, and we thought that this should be based on agreement. I can tell you about all the proposals that were bandied about, 30 kilometres, five kilometres, the width of a bus, and what have you not. All sorts of proposals. And then for aircraft to fly over. People were coming up with all sorts of things. But the basic idea was that we should have a corridor linking up the two ethnic territories, the two Serb territories, Semberija and Krajina. And it was supposed to be based on an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You said all sorts of proposals were being bandied about. You mean, do you, at the talks between you and the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. We had some contacts with the deputies probably, if that's what I remember, when this assembly was held. Perhaps there was a break too, I don't know. And then everybody was saying what was necessary, that it should go up to the Sava River and there should be 30 kilometres or five kilometres or the width of a bus so that a bus could get through. And so on and so forth. It wasn't at the session itself. It was in the corridors. When you're chatting to people, when you're talking to people, and when you hear these proposals.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In the discussions that you told the Trial Chamber you had already had with the Croats, at Graz particularly, at which the question of a corridor had come up, what discussion had there been there about the size of this corridor?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked to the Croat side primarily about regrouping these Serb ethnic areas in Posavina and the Croat areas. If we have Serb areas up to the Sava we would concede that to the Croats and then they would give us this area that would be the corridor. We talked about their interest in certain points. So Kupres was mentioned. In principle, we agreed that that should be an agreement that should be reached later. Of course, we cannot have a corridor without the agreement of the third side, because there is this narrow belt where this imaginary corridor went through Muslim territory as well. So we would have to achieve that too, but, of course, if you resolve four-fifths with the Croats, then there is just this one little thing left to discuss with the Muslims, and after all, the Croat side was not in charge of the area around Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So was it -- was it the broad understanding at the Graz talks that through what was regarded as Croat territory, this corridor would be at least many kilometres wide as opposed to the very narrow type of corridor that allowed just the width of a bus?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was speaking figuratively when I said a bus but I remember that there was a proposal like that in actual fact. We were speaking in general terms. We did not want to set this in stone, how big the corridor would be. We would see how many of these blue areas we had, so to speak, and how many brown ones and then we would reach an agreement ultimately. We would find a solution. The basic thing that the Croats agreed upon was that they understood our problem, and that they were willing for us to reach an agreement in that respect. What kind of agreement? That would be dealt with subsequently. There is something I forgot to mention here, forgot to tell the Honourable Trial Chamber and all the others. We then talked about our right to access to the sea. I mean, this was in Graz. That's what we discussed in Graz. Because Bosnia did have access. I forgot all about that. The representative of Croatia was there too and they said, "We will talk about that later, between Croatia and Bosnia and we will work out some kind of arrangement" but the Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina could not pass any kind of judgement on that. I remember that now that you asked me this other question. So the width was not agreed upon with the Croat side, I mean the width of the corridor, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When -- on your side, those discussions in Graz, did you have in mind a corridor of at least many kilometres' width?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We did have in mind a corridor that should be -- well, not to have just a path, to have a reasonable type of corridor. It can best be seen on a map that we drew where we talked about this. That is in Mr. Owen's book as well, exactly what this corridor should look like, the one that we kept talking about. This is going through somebody else's territory. It would be our territory but it's not territory that would be used actually. It would just serve the purpose of passing through it but then it wouldn't just be the road. You would have a bit of land on the side as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, at this point, I wonder if you could be given two items which we've notified, the first is P68, tab 16, and the other is the P47 that I mentioned a few minutes ago. I can see from here that that's the right item, Mr. Krajisnik. Now, this is -- this was produced by Mr. Treanor. You probably remember this. This was his map just in a fairly simple form, indicating the six strategic objectives and then in English, on his map, the six strategic objectives as they were later set out in the Official Gazette, which is, among other things, why I would like you to have P47, because that's the Serbian version of what the rest of us have in English on Mr. Treanor's map. So what you have is P47 so far as I'm aware, Mr. Krajisnik, is exactly what we see in English on -- in that block on Mr. Treanor's map. First of all, are you -- you -- there have been lots that Mr. Treanor's said that you don't agree with, Mr. Krajisnik. That would never come as a surprise to me or anybody else. But so far as Mr. Treanor's map is concerned, are you satisfied that it does at least indicate clearly where these objectives lay on the ground and is at least an accurate summary of, if you like, the issues?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there are some major mistakes that require explanation, especially the Neretva River valley and the Drina, and also access to the sea. It is not well defined. It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. Let's narrow it down, then, Mr. Krajisnik. Objective 1 can't conveniently be shown on the map and hasn't been shown on the map. Objective 2, you didn't mention any particular difficulty with that. It's -- in very bare terms, that's the location of that particular issue is correctly shown on the map, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Right. It would link up Krajina and Semberija. It would be a bit further up but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik -- it's very simplified of course. Objective 5 is just stated. There is nothing that arises out of the description of that objective on this map, is there? It's simply tells us where Sarajevo is and says that that was objective 5. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You have -- as far as this map is concerned, where you take issue and we are going to come to those objectives is on numbers 3, 5 and 6, just trying to narrow it down. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. 3, 4 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, my slip of the tongue. I beg your pardon. 3, 4 and 6. My mistake. 3, 4 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Just wanted to narrow it down, then, Mr. Krajisnik. So let's look again then at the assembly minute and see what Mr. Krajisnik -- Mr. Karadzic, rather, is saying about the third strategic goal. Page 13 of the English. Page 7 of the Serbian. "The third strategic goal is to establish a corridor in the Drina valley, that is elimination of the Drina as a border between two worlds. We are on both sides of the Drina and our strategic interest and our living space are there. We now see a possibility of some Muslim municipalities to be set up along the Drina as enclaves in order for them to achieve their rites but that belt along the Drina must basically belong to Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina, as much as it is strategically useful for us in a positive way, it helps us, by damaging the interests of our enemy in establishing a corridor which would connect them to the Muslim international and render this area permanently unstable." Mr. Krajisnik, at the time of this assembly meeting, can you say, were you content with that description by Dr. Karadzic of the third strategic goal?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not content. I believe he wasn't content either. Especially with this second part of the explanation. Because he wanted to say that enclaves would be there and then he added, well, Republika Srpska, but it can't be our enclaves if -- if it's going to be other ethnic communities. Quite simply, he didn't want the MPs from that part of Republika Srpska to be opposed to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I'm going to have to ask you perhaps to clarify a bit of that answer. Where you said then he added, well, Republika Srpska but it can't be our enclaves if it's going to be other ethnic communities, are you -- are you saying that what -- what Dr. Karadzic is recorded as having said here is -- inaccurately expresses what you understood to be the third strategic goal?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO KRAJISNIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic said that by attaining this objective of having a corridor in the valley of the Drina River, not on the Drina, as it says here, that in that corridor, and that can be seen in our proposal too, the one that we gave to Mr. Cutileiro, that's where the enclaves would be, the Muslim enclaves. We can already see that, Srebrenica, Zepa, and I don't know, doesn't matter. He is saying that the Drina cannot -- well, that the whole belt cannot be Serbian, and there should have been a full stop there. But he went on, explaining, so that he would pre-empt the possibility of other discussions. These enclaves would be part of Republika Srpska. But he knew according to the Cutileiro plan, this belonged to the other ethnic community and it would have to be resolved in a different way, either through exchanges or through annexation or that their ethnic community would consist of several parts. Well, I don't agree with that. He doesn't agree with that either but that's the way he put it. So this is not the corridor. This is the border. This is the Drina River. And the corridor was envisaged elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, could we please invite Mr. Krajisnik to take the pointer and tell us exactly what in his view now this objective 3 was? Establish a corridor on the Drina River valley, eliminating the Drina as a border separating Serbian states. Now, we see that the northern part of the Drina is separating at this moment Bosnia and Herzegovina from Serbia. The more southerly part is within Bosnia and Herzegovina. Yes. When we are talking about the Drina River valley, are we talking about the whole of it or are we talking about the southern part only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give me another map, if possible, the one with blue and green, and then I'll tell you precisely. Or the Cutileiro plan, give me that and then I'll show you exactly. You can't see anything here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as long as the rivers are in the right place, I think, Mr. Krajisnik, you should be able to explain to us what this would result in finally. Perhaps we have another copy of this map which we could then use so we know that objective 3 has got something to do with the Drina, so to that extent it doesn't -- it doesn't disturb the exercise, the same for the Neretva, it just says, Neretva, objective 4, and for the Una, objective 4 as well. Would there be any spare copy of this map? Because this one is in evidence. Yes, I see that Mr. Harmon has a spare copy. Perhaps the other one to be taken from the -- is this the original? Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, if you would take a black -- perhaps first with the pointer or with the pen and then we'll invite you to make any markings when it has become clear enough to us. Could you try to explain on the basis of this map and just concentrate on the municipalities we have over there, you could explain to us where there were any majority-Muslim or majority-Serb municipalities, what did you understand by exactly by a border separating Serbian states and which states you had in mind. Could you please guide us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please explain the entire objective? This corridor is supposed to be here, between Semberija and Romanija. That should be the corridor. And you see this is Serbian territory. This is the Drina but the territory is Serb. Only with this part does Bosnia border with Serbia. This is the border of Bosnia. There is no Drina River here. So what it says here? That Drina should not be the border between two worlds. That's what it says. Up to here, the Drina is the border between Bosnia and Serbia, whereas up here, there is a Serb enclave and Serbia. So that's not what was being referred to. And down here the Drina is not on the border with Serbia. So what we wanted was to link up the Serb territories. You will see on the Cutileiro man and on our map that there should be a corridor in the Drina River valley and it's marked there, whereas the Neretva --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We would like to have the other map there as well. That is the coloured map with the ethnicities indicated so that we know more or less what are majority.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The big one with the orange and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's P211, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not this map, no, no. That's the whole municipality. Could I please have the other map, where those parts are? I have the map here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you show us which map you have in mind, then -- that's the one you'd like to have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can better explain it with that map, we'll give you an opportunity. That's 293.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before we -- perhaps before we leave or whether we return to the map we were just using, I would not wish to return to the footage of today's session in order to accurately identify those portions that Mr. Krajisnik was pointing to. I understood the Court was going to--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll try to do my utmost best to have everything clear on the record but not until after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, would you prefer to deal with the number 10, paragraph number 10 provided by Mr. Krajisnik now or rather do it at a later stage? It has been distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I think we would rather do it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we leave it for the time being and go back to the Drina River. I do understand that we have now the different map. Mr. Krajisnik, you said you could better explain it to us on the basis of that map. Please tell us where exactly -- what I'm a bit concerned about is whether the maps are -- looks a bit stretched in the north-south directions rather than to get the right proportions but I haven't got a copy with me at this point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be positioned a bit better here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have a slightly different concern, Your Honour, but no doubt Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please -- yes, could you please put the map in such a way on the ELMO -- yes, I see that the dimensions, north, west, east -- north, south, east, west seem to be different from any other maps we've seen, I don't know what happened with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It clearly has got stretched north south. If I can just mention my own concern, if Mr. Krajisnik just bears it in mind, it may be shared by others, this strategic objective is defined by reference to a river, and explanation by reference to a map on which the river is impossible to see, wouldn't seem perfect. So, if Mr. Krajisnik would just please have that in mind when he goes through the explanation, it might be clearer as we go along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, the Judges have in front of them still also P68, 16, which gives us the rivers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, indeed Your Honours, we have that but if Mr. Krajisnik would just please bear that in mind having regard to the place at which we go through this explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger wants to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I hope this is helpful. In any event, I have an extra copy of P293 which is large. It can be marked on if the Court requests so but I wanted the court to know this is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have some competing maps. If you show to Mr. Krajisnik exactly what -- you have P293? Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, there is a large one which seems not to be distorted, as a matter of fact. If markings would be better made on that map, could you -- Madam Usher, could you please show it to Mr. Krajisnik? If that would be better for your purposes, Mr. Krajisnik, then it's easier to mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same map. It's the same map. It's not elongated here either. Only it's not elongated here, the map here, I think it's something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's distorted on the screen. If you say, "I can work on the map that you've got at the moment please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can I just ask Your Honour whether this map we have been using, P93, is a reduced version of the original or whether what Mr. Tieger just produced is a blown-up version of the original? Which is the -- which is the original map? Is it the big one or the small one is my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik may explain on the basis of the map he has in front of him the matter and let's now proceed. Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The original maps were like this one and these are reduced maps, sized down, and the gentlemen in the Office of the Prosecutor have the original maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik if you can work on the map that's now on the ELMO, please proceed. Let's stop talking much more about -- yes, before you mark, please explain. Yes? The corridor was supposed to be from where to where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Along -- you mean the Drina corridor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Drina corridor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will say: Roughly, the corridor was supposed to go like this. Along these blue lines, and possibly to have an exchange of territories --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Exchange is a later state. I first want to know where the corridor was. You started connecting and I'm trying now to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would go through our own territories and here, where there are some villages, we would try to link up with Semberija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take a black pen and draw a line which would be at the centre of the corridor you had in mind, so the centre of the corridor, and later I'll ask to you make a dotted line where approximately the bell -- borders of the corridor would be. So could you first take the core of what was to be the corridor, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we did not define where the corridor would run. We only said how, through our territory, and that's along the Drina River valley. As for the precise route that would be a matter of agreement and exchange of territories. We would not go through somebody else's territory. That's why this map would be better. That's all I wanted to say. We wouldn't be going through here or through here but through this area, and then we would try, in a planned way, to exchange and where there is a bypass, to go that way. This was something that was to be agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then before making any markings, could you explain to us where you found potential obstacles, where you would find territory of others which you would not want to include? Where were the problematic parts? Could you please point at them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wherever there is the Muslim green colour along the route. For example, here. And maybe we could squeeze through. But there would be an obstacle here and it would have to be exchanged for those territories which would perhaps be left for the Muslims. But I'm saying all this off the top of my head now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We are all aware that we are not talking about a precisely defined corridor but a corridor to be situated approximately there. So I would -- is there another copy of this map available? Because I'm going to do it in a totally different way. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The best logistics we have is through the Office of the Prosecutor. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My next question: What I'm going to do is I'm trying to understand what you tell us. I'm trying to mark that on a copy of this map myself. And then at a later stage, you'll see whether the drawing is of any success or where it should be adjusted and then we might make a new one with your adjustments. One further question: When you said where approximately the corridor should be, you went approximately to the level of Sarajevo, little bit south. I take it that's what you call Romanija. In the beginning you went even further south. Would the corridor stretch even further south as well or would it stop at the Sarajevo level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were only talking about between Romanija and Semberija. That's the Drina, from Romanija upwards. That was that strategic objective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I'll now try, you'll later see what the result is, to approximately indicate where there was a need for a corridor. Could you again tell us where you saw potential obstacles? I think you pointed at a place just northwest of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Either we would squeeze through here, where there are blue lines, or we would search here, depending on what we achieved through negotiations and agreement but there is an obstacle here, you can see that on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll then encircle approximately the area of the first obstacle. Any other obstacle on the way to Romanija? I see further south there is a larger portion of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Romanija, Your Honour. And down here, this is not part of the strategic objective down here. But from Romanija one would have to go up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I see there is another patch of not really blue. You would go to the -- would you consider that to be a potential obstacle as well? And I'm looking now at the area just southeast of Olovo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see there is access to the Drina here. Here there are Serb territories. So it would all be open to discussion. Our aim was to link this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So most important was to create a link. Now we have the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ilijas, I would say close to the Drina river, east from Sarajevo, where we find patches, yes. Those areas, what were the plans with those areas? And I'm talking from Srebrenica to Visegrad and Gorazde. There you will find some non-blue. Could you please point at Srebrenica? A little bit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Srebrenica. This is the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac. This is Zepa and this is Srebrenica and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First let's concentrate on Srebrenica and Bratunac. What was the intention to do with that area, which is only partly blue and is also a relatively light blue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A small municipality was formed here called Skelani and it was part of Srebrenica municipality. Certainly, a much smaller area here would be Serbian and a far larger part would be Muslim, because there is a lot more green here than blue. Skelani -- well, this perhaps would be Serbian, the municipality of Skelani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So to say that the most easterly part of Srebrenica municipality would then be Skelani, I'll make a circle around that on my map and mark that with a 2. Okay. Now we go further south, Visegrad seems to be also very much a non-Serb, I take it Muslim, part, Visegrad, where we are now on the eastern side of the Neretva River. What was intended --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] East of the Drina, yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes, east of the Drina. Very much by colour Muslim. What did the third strategic objective had in mind for this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Cutileiro plan, this part, Rudo, Cajnice, and this part would belong to the Serbs and all the rest to the Muslims. Visegrad itself --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless you say that the Cutileiro plan in this respect reflected the strategic objectives completely, I'd like you to answer the question on what the strategic objectives were doing with this part, unless you say it was not -- well, it was not elaborated yet in such a detail but I'd like to know what in accordance with the strategic objective number 3, what would happen with the Visegrad and Rudo municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the basis for the strategic objectives was the Cutileiro map. If you look at it, you will see where Semberija and Romanija would be linked up, where there are Serb areas and where there are Muslim areas. That was our objective. You will see that there precisely. That was the basis. It was open to negotiation, of course, because we had interruptions or obstacles in two places on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the problem with the Cutileiro map is that there are several Cutileiro maps but I'll invite Mr. Registrar to provide me with I think it's D4 or D5, D6, and if you would please tell me which would be the best one to consult to better understand the strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is only one Cutileiro map. The others are ours. There are four maps. There are Muslim, Serb, Croat maps, and the Cutileiro map. Ours has more Serb territories. The Cutileiro map has smaller Serb territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think it may be D7, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to be sure, D7, not D7B?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Well, looking at the list, it's D7A and D7B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes that brings me again to the problem that I can't copy something from two maps at the same time. Which one, Mr. Krajisnik, which one would be the better one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That one is the Cutileiro map, the one in your right-hand is the Muslim map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I then work on 7B, which is the -- which seems to say in Cyrillic, Cutileiro map on the bottom. So -- yes. Now I see on the Cutileiro map that the part of Srebrenica you just said you would like to have as a Serb territory, that was the eastern part, is on the Cutileiro map not Serb but for the remainder, I do understand that -- and I'll try to do that as good as I can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since you asked me about the corridor, I showed the blue patch and said that was Skelani municipality which had been set up. I didn't say it would be part of the corridor. It's far from the corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say the corridor is only that. Okay. Then that portion I would say the Visegrad, Cajnice, Rudo area, I more or less, although not in every detail, copied that from the Cutileiro map, although it continues but I only took that specific part and without any details. Now the corridor is clear to me. I know approximately what happens in the -- on the area east from -- east from the Drina river. Now, could you explain, perhaps on the basis of the map that is in front of you, exactly where was the problem of -- I'll have to -- part of objective 3 is that the Drina should be eliminated as a border separating Serbian states. Could you clearly explain to us where changes were needed or perhaps not changes but where the problem was of the Drina separating -- the Drina as a border separating Serbian states? Could you please do that on the basis of the map which is on the ELMO? Because I now concentrate on the -- first of all, on the northern part of the Drina where it bends to the east, and before it bends back to the west, or I should say the other way because it's flowing from south to north, I think. Yes. In the northern part I would say up to -- from Bijeljina, Zvornik, Bratunac, there the Drina forms the border between Serbia proper and to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Was there an issue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I'll explain right now. In the Cutileiro plan, you have the constituent units, and we had the right to special links with the neighbouring republics of Serbia and Montenegro, so we wouldn't need passports, there wouldn't be a real border. I gave -- the speech made by Mr. Izetbegovic in December 1991, who said Drina must never be a border for the Serbs and Croats in Bosnia, however we set up Bosnia. The Drina should not be a border between worlds. Later on, in the strategic objectives, the word was "states" so it wasn't about the map, it was about the right to have links, apart from statehood we could have links in culture, education and so on which would not be to the detriment of the integrity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You can see that in the Cutileiro plan. That's what this sentence means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I see in the Cutileiro plan that in the northern part of the border between Serbia proper and Bosnia and Herzegovina, as a whole, that up to approximately Zvornik, the territory west of the Drina would become Serb, and at the other side of the river, we would find Serbia proper, so the Drina would there not -- I mean it would have united Serb, Bosnian Serb, although the Drina river was flowing there, or is that a wrong understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, that's not what it was about. There would be a border here between Bosnia and Yugoslavia but the border would not be visible. There would be no passports. One could pass through, and that is enshrined in the written part of the Cutileiro plan and today in the Dayton Accord so we would have dual nationality, we could have links in culture, education and so on. But not as a state. That was the meaning of this sentence. There would be a border crossing. The Serbs would be -- there would be Serbs in Serbia and Serbs here. We could cross the border in Srebrenica, in Rudo, anywhere. But Drina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I do understand. So although the Drina was there the administrative border between two states, nevertheless it would be hardly visible. Would that mean that the border control, et cetera, would move westwards to where you would enter the territory of I now say Muslim Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is would there be some border control? Would there be no border control at all any more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The administrative border of Bosnia-Herzegovina that existed in Yugoslavia would become the state border, and it would be just like any other border that's easy to cross, just as in the European Union, you don't have to have a visa and so on. That's what we wanted, the border would not be visible. It wouldn't be the kind of border where you needed a passport. And that was enshrined in every agreement and the Croats agreed to this, they liked it, and the Muslims accepted it. And you can see that in the principles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that part of eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina that on the basis of the Cutileiro map would become Muslim, and I'm now talking about more or less the area between Zvornik and Bratunac, where Muslim territory would be separated by the Drina river from Yugoslavia or Serbia proper, would there also be no border control and would it also be an invisible, although existing, administrative border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every national unit would have the right to have special connections. It would apply to everyone. Today, there is Bosnia and Yugoslavia. Our goal was for the psychological border on the Drina not to be there for the Serbs. It was a problem for centuries, especially -- well, there is no problem concerning Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. It's not a direct answer to my question. Part of the eastern border of the state, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and mainly between Zvornik and, well, it goes even further than Bratunac, Srebrenica, that portion in the -- on the Cutileiro map, would be Muslim. Was it left to the Muslims whether they would have any visible border control for the population or was it up to them to agree that with Yugoslavia or was it foreseen that there should not be a visible border there as well? Because I do understand that further up north, and further south, although further south it's not -- the Drina is not -- is not the border, but further up north, there should be no visible border, although everyone knew that to the west of the river it would be Serb territory or territory of a Serb entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and to the east it would be Yugoslavia, but should there be no visible border either on that portion where the Muslims were controlling the territory which was at the border and was at the Drina river or would you leave that to the Muslims themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this would be regulated, but the Muslim constituent unit would have the right to reach an agreement on crossing the border with Serbia. Now, how they would regulate it, and in which way, that would be an agreement between their constituent unit and Serbia. We would regulate it where we have territory. Today, there is a single border control service, but then it was envisaged that every constituent unit should control the border. You know why this would particularly be the case? Because Sandzak is on the other side is on the other side and it suits the Muslims to have a soft border there, so to speak. It's not that there would not be a border anywhere. It would be a soft border where you could cross any way you wanted to but it would be known who is where. We were just talking on behalf of the Serb side, not on behalf of the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's now perfectly clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'm just worried about your map, Mr. President. I wonder whether you drew it well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please -- I may have to look that up. The eastern part of Srebrenica, that would be municipality of -- you gave the name. I've forgotten. That portion would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Skelani, Skelani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Skelani, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was always a municipality except that it's been done away with now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But it did not exist in the Cutileiro plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I just marked it as Skelani because you explained that in your testimony and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This map does not depict the whole of the story, but just illustrates what we understood to be your testimony. Could it be put on the ELMO? Only the eastern part of the map is relevant. Okay. What I tried to do is to say approximately what area should be linked through that corridor, Semberija in the north and Romanija in the south, not giving any details as to where exactly to locate that. I indicated under 1 as a potential obstacle as you said still to be resolved one way or another to find your way through so that there would be -- that it would really be a corridor. Under 2, I indicated the municipality of Skelani, which perhaps the Serbs may have wished but certainly would not become Serb in the Cutileiro plan, and then in 3, I worked a little bit further south. It ends in nothing but, of course, in the Cutileiro we have that, we can see that it continues. But to know that in that area in the Cutileiro plan it would be Serb. And I'm not talking about any details. And now I understood that most important for the Drina not to be a border between Serbian states is that it would, although a state border, it would be, as you called it, a soft border, allowing for free movement, no control, exchange culturally, whatever way, and in the area between -- between Zvornik and Bratunac, which would be a border where, on the west side, there was Muslim territory, that you left it to the Muslims how soft or how non-soft that border would be. Is that a correct understanding? And I'm not talking about details but just about --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The essence of it is there but the corridor would go this way. It's not that this part would be taken because there is a big Muslim enclave. So it will go this way, here. That would be it. So that is just a small objection. But at any rate, it would be our territories that would be linked up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then if you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President, I'm sorry, and there would be a bit lower, you know it would be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I tried to copy that. I did not perfectly copy that from the Cutileiro map but it's intended to represent what you find on the Cutileiro map. So let's say if you could give me -- could I have the map back for one second again? Could it be put on the ELMO again? Now I'll formulate it in a different way. Between these dotted lines, the corridor would find its way from Semberija in whatever way and I now made it a bit wider in the south, would find its way still to be defined from north to south or south to north linking Semberija with Romanija.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Semberija would be linked up this way. Well, then it would be precise. It wouldn't go all the way out here. That would be too far away. I mean, this would be too far out to the west. Couldn't be done that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's mainly for our understanding and I do understand that where I made the dotted line to the east a wit wider, it should be a little bit moved, and that the other dotted line, that is the western dotted line should be a little bit more to the east, especially in the southern part of it. Yes. Well, I think that we now fully grab --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour, it would go this way, yes, here, where the Serb territories are only so that there would be as little exchange of territory as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is not an expert map or anything but it's just an instrument which helped us to better understand what exactly strategic objective 3 was. I don't know whether we have similar problems with the other part of strategic objective 3. I think it's far less. But I would leave that to Mr. Stewart. Yes, Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Skelani, over here, I added that. That was not in the strategic objective. I added that. I said that it had been established as a municipality. Only this is the strategic objective. And that the Drina should be a soft border. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that becomes clear from the testimony itself, and therefore I didn't add anything to Skelani apart from that that's Skelani and your testimony was clear on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, perhaps this should be marked as a Chamber exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: TC 1 or I don't know what the convention is.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be C 2, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: C, is it? Same idea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, if it's going to be marked, then it has to be corrected a bit. It wouldn't be good for this part to remain this way, it should be the other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... suggestion for that, Your Honour, because Mr. Krajisnik was without marking indicating corrections. I wonder if we perhaps might invite Mr. Krajisnik to do some homework and produce --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. As a matter of fact I think I now perfectly understood. It's not about details. I'll make another one which is clearer and then adjusting everything I'll just copy from here, I'll take a bit more precisely the Cutileiro and then we don't have any further discussions on it because it just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, provided Mr. Krajisnik then is completely happy with it, Your Honour, because with -- Your Honour's help is greatly appreciated but Mr. Krajisnik indicated a moment ago his reservation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Krajisnik is not happy with it we'll see what to do and, of course, we are all trying to make Mr. Krajisnik happy in this respect. Let's move --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour -- it was why I was suggesting, if Mr. Krajisnik were to produce the version overnight that he is happy with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I took a different course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour is the Judge or one of the Judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have no time left apart from two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour could I -- on P293, Your Honour, it did have a point, Your Honour, my inquiry about the size. If the original map is the larger one, that's the one that should go in evidence, Your Honour. It's a difficult map to use any way and if the original is that larger version, we would suggest that is the one that ought to go into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the smaller one is in evidence. It has been used before. We leave that. If you feel that there is any need to also have the larger one admitted into evidence, we'll hear the specific reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not such a big deal. I would be grateful to have a larger one any way if at all possible. It's not an easy map to use, this little one. But that's just a request. The Prosecution have got that map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As you said, Mr. Stewart, and rightly so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You rightly said that I'm the Judge, one of the Judges. Mr. Krajisnik, if you would limit yourself to putting at that map what I did, but then make the right dotted lines with a red pen, I don't know whether you have a red pen, otherwise you can borrow the red pen of the Chamber, you're invited to do it better than I did, so overnight, if you could, but please limit yourself to what I put on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just say something, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood you. It was my understanding that this map was just for your understanding, that the corridor goes along the Serb territories, that we did not define it, but that it would be subject to negotiations, and that now you drew this in order to understand what it was that I was saying. So we are going along these Serb territories linking up Semberija and Romanija. That is why this map does not have to be admitted if you understood what I meant by strategic objective. Because what I draw is not correct. It's not that we drew this map. That is why this is how you understand our linking up of Semberija and Romanija, along our territories, and when there is a problem it should resolved by way of agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, the problem might be in the future, the Appeals Chamber. They have to know what we did exactly. I suggest the following. You keep for the time being that map. You'll be provided with a -- you'll be provided with an empty map of the same map but not marked. We'll leave it up to you to consider overnight whether you can make, especially the dotted lines, a bit more precise. If you do so, you're invited to do it either clearly on the existing map and then tomorrow we'll decide on admission of this map. If you'd prefer to copy the markings but more accurately on the empty copy, then you're invited to do so with the red marker but also please be aware that there should be -- nothing else be marked on it apart from what I marked on the map. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me do it straight away. I'll do it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, because the other court is waiting, I take it. So we have to finish for the day, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. It goes without saying that I get to keep the marker, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, you can borrow ours and that's a red one. Mr. Krajisnik, it will not often happen that you will do the red marking because usually for the Defence it's the black marking. So exceptionally, although you as a witness did the marking, it is -- you may do it in red. I do understand that a copy has been given to Mr. Registrar to be provided to you, Mr. Krajisnik, with the C -- no, I'm -- you'll receive what you're supposed to receive through Mr. Registrar. Then we adjourn until Wednesday, tomorrow, Courtroom II, 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
